title: PRISM prioritization rubric for inference roadmap
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce PRISM, a multidimensional prioritization rubric tailored for Redwood Inference's product roadmap. PRISM stands for Prioritization Value, Risk, Impact (latency & cost), Speed to Value, and Margins. The goal is to provide a repeatable, auditable scoring process that complements RICE-style signals with explicit latency/cost normalization and a deployability risk multiplier. PRISM is intended for scoring initiatives across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private product lines and to feed the OKR/initiative tracker for quarterly planning.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical PRISM spec published in Confluence with scoring formulas
Scoring spreadsheet with normalized latency and cost inputs for top 30 candidate initiatives
Integration shim that exports PRISM scores to the roadmap tool (CSV/JSON)
Stakeholder sign-off from Product, Eng, and Solutions (written in ticket comments)
Baseline dashboard in Console showing PRISM score components for live initiatives

notes: Scoring summary: final_score = (P * I * S * M) * (1 - R) where P=PrioritizationValue(0-10), I=ImpactNormalized(0-10), S=SpeedWeight(0.5-1.5), M=MarginsFactor(0.5-1.5), R=RiskMultiplier(0-0.6)
Latency normalization: map p50 and p95 to 0-10 band using historical percentile distributions for similar features (transform: log-latency -> z-score -> clamp)
Cost normalization: convert GPU and token costs to $/1k tokens, then to relative impact on unit economics; use Finance-defined thresholds for 0-10 mapping
Risk calculation: weighted sum of DeployComplexity, BackwardsCompat, ObservabilityGap; high ObservabilityGap increases R by +0.15 to force remediation before high-impact launches
Example: Dedicated-autoscaler tested: P=8, I=7, S=1.2, M=1.1, R=0.12 => score ~ 64.7 (prioritized for Q2 canary)
